item.title: Exact nonstationary heat-excess statistics in the weakly asymmetric Kipnis--Marchioro--Presutti model
item.description: arXiv:2611.31303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exact nonstationary large-deviation statistics remain scarce for interacting many-body systems. Here we employ the macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT) to determine the complete long-time statistics of heat excess produced by an initially localized heat pulse in the weakly asymmetric Kipnis--Marchioro--Presutti model. We find a remarkable nonlocal canonical transformation which maps the weakly asymmetric MFT problem, including its initial and terminal conditions, onto the symmetric problem, previously solved exactly. The resulting rate function is an explicit nonlinear deformation of its symmetric counterpart. We also extend the solution to heat measured beyond an arbitrary observation point.
item.dc:creator: Baruch Meerson

item.title: Condensates and Edge Effects in the Generalised Takayasu Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.31325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, in the 1D Takayasu Mass Model (MM) of diffusion-aggregation with input, large condensates and a novel power law were observed in simulations, and later characterised exactly. We extend these studies to the Takayasu model with generalised input, and provide a relation to translate the distribution function of the MM to any model with a space and time independent injection process. In the 1D Charge Model (CM) of a system of size $L$, where $q=+1$ and $-1$ charge monomers are injected with equal probability at each site in each time step, there is a power law distribution of cluster charge $P(q)\sim |q|^{-5/3}$. This distribution cuts off at $|q|\sim L^{3/2}$ in the steady state for long times $t\gg L^2$ and a large charge condensate forms with a net charge between $-\sqrt{Lt}$ and $\sqrt{Lt}$. A distance dependent distribution function is observed around the charge condensate and near open boundaries, both of which act like an edge in the system, analogous to the observations in the MM. The charge distribution measured at a distance $x$ from the edge transitions from the previously known CM bulk power law $P(q)\sim |q|^{-5/3}$ for small clusters ($|q|< x^{3/2}$), to a novel power law $P(q)\sim |q|^{-7/3}$ for larger clusters ($|q|>x^{3/2}$). In the 1D Pair Injection Model (PIM), where $+1$ and $-1$ charge monomers are injected simultaneously at adjacent sites, the power law distribution $P(q)\sim |q|^{-2}$ cuts off at $|q|\sim L$ in the steady state for long times, and no large growing condensate is formed. We still observe a distance dependent distribution measured from the largest clusters, or an open boundary, with a bulk power law $P(q)\sim |q|^{-2}$ for small clusters ($|q|< x$), and an edge power law $P(q)\sim |q|^{-3}$ for larger clusters ($|q >x$).
item.dc:creator: Angad Singh

item.title: What time is it in Assembly Space? Cronin and Walker's "The Physics of Causation" fails elementary dimensional analysis (Comment on arXiv:2601.00515)
item.description: arXiv:2611.31339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cronin and Walker claim that causation is quantified by an ``assembly index'', a count of the steps needed to build an object. Remarkably, they equate ``continuous time (as measured by clocks)'' to a multiple of the index, which is a dimensionless number. Their argument treats one parameter as simultaneously a rate, a time interval, and a pure number, and provides no timescale to convert index to clock time. This dimensional incoherence betrays, at best, an ill-conceived and ill-formed theory, and fatally undermines two central claims. First, the exponential weighting at the heart of what they call the assembly equation can be obtained only by supplying a timescale, which they never do, or by recasting clock time as a dimensionless count of assembly steps. In the latter case, their ``derivation'' trivially reduces to Bernoulli's seventeenth-century compound-interest limit. Second, lacking rates or energy scales, their account cannot predict how quickly, or under what conditions, anything forms, and yet formation ``in finite time'' is their criterion for distinguishing spontaneous from ``selected'' objects. Assembly theory is thus incapable of addressing causation.
item.dc:creator: Philip Moriarty

item.title: Localization in one-dimensional magnetic quasicrystals
item.description: arXiv:2611.31384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The celebrated Aubry-Andr\'e-Harper model undergoes a metal-insulator transition akin to Anderson localization due to an energetic competition between nearest-neighbor hopping and a quasiperiodic on-site potential. In this work, we consider the problem of a one-dimensional lattice subject to a quasiperiodic external field, where the topology of the underlying graph mediates the competition between insulating and conducting phases. In particular, we present examples for which all dispersive eigenstates are critically localized, as well as models in which they are exponentially localized. We also demonstrate the coexistence of these phenomena with an extensive set of degenerate finitely supported eigenstates forming a flat band. Finally, we construct models with exactly solvable mobility edges arising only from graph structure. Going beyond these single-particle results, we show---using exact-diagonalization calculations of the bosonic dynamics---that, as in the conventional Aubry-Andr\'e-Harper case, on-site interactions drive localized eigenstates toward extendedness. Our results provide a framework for exploring how magnetic interference and interactions jointly constrain transport in quasiperiodic lattices.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Osborne, Rhine Samajdar, Andrew A. Houck

item.title: From Growth Inhibition to Fluctuations: Testing an Ising Model of Bacterial Responses to Antibiotics
item.description: arXiv:2611.31609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Complex networks of biochemical reactions have been proposed to exhibit emergent cooperativity that can be described by an effective Ising model, with a small number of parameters encoding collective interactions. Here this mapping is experimentally tested using the response of three bacterial species to a range of antibiotics acting on different cellular targets. The Ising description is compared to the conventional Hill model, examining both the mean growth-rate response and, importantly, its population growth-rate heterogeneity (PGRH). While both models describe the mean growth-rate dependence on antibiotic concentration comparably well, we find that the Ising model provides a markedly better description of PGRH, offering an additional and more stringent test of the collective description. The fitted Ising interaction strength is systematically related to the Hill exponent and increases with the functional distance of the antibiotic target from the protein-production machinery. These results provide experimental support for describing complex biochemical reaction networks through effective cooperative Ising interactions, and suggest that the collective response of bacterial growth to antibiotics reflects the organization of the underlying metabolic network.
item.dc:creator: Pietro Cicuta, Morten Kals, Nir S. Gov

item.title: Upper and lower bounds for the critical point of the three-dimensional Ising model
item.description: arXiv:2611.31872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the critical point $K_c$ of the nearest-neighbour Ising ferromagnet on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ satisfies $0.2164203058<K_c<0.2293910295$, equivalently $1.541630483<e^{2K_c}<1.582145851$, with both endpoints given by explicit rational numbers. To our knowledge these are the sharpest rigorous bounds available. They improve the classical bounds of Fisher (1967) and of Fr\"ohlich, Simon and Spencer (1976), narrowing the rigorously known interval by a factor of about 3.5, and the interval contains the numerical estimate of the critical point. For the lower bound we refine Fisher's self-avoiding-walk argument. A shortest path in the high-temperature expansion forbids all bonds spanned by its vertices, and the resulting gain is estimated through local correlation integrals and summed over paths by a finite-memory transfer bound. As a by-product, the connective constant of $\mathbb{Z}^3$ is shown to be at most $4.73195$. For the upper bound we prove an infrared bound whose coefficient involves the nearest-neighbour correlation. We keep the zero Fourier mode as an unknown and force it to be positive by exact local relations for the spins on a small shell. The finite inequalities entering the proof are verified in exact rational arithmetic, and the passage to the thermodynamic limit is proved analytically.
item.dc:creator: Zhongpu Qiu

item.title: Exact Response Theory based on Karhunen-Lo\`eve Expansions for Brownian Oscillators
item.description: arXiv:2611.32038v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend Exact Response Theory (ERT) to an overdamped Brownian oscillator driven by thermal white noise. The stochastic forcing is represented by a Karhunen--Lo\`eve series and embedded into an autonomous, augmented phase space using a harmonic auxiliary phase. This representation allows us to construct the ERT dissipation function for fixed mode amplitudes and recover stochastic averages by averaging over the amplitudes and the initial phase. For the variance, we derive the response at finite spectral truncation and show analytically that, with uniform phase sampling, the full-spectrum white-noise limit reproduces the generator-based result for a sudden temperature change. Furthermore, a comparison with first-order linear response theory highlights how this may fail in general. In particular, if the noise-induced variance is quadratic in the noise amplitude, it is completely omitted by linear response. The analysis provides a framework for this model and for studying more general forcing; extensions to non-Markovian dynamics require separate convergence and regularity analyses.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Colangeli, Lamberto Rondoni, Pasquale Vozza

item.title: Network topology imposes spectral constraints on collective nonequilibrium responses
item.description: arXiv:2611.32130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Collective nonequilibrium dynamics in Langevin systems depend on both network topology and stochastic driving. Understanding the role of topology in responses to stochastic driving and in the emergence of nonequilibrium is essential. Starting from the principle of microscopic reversibility and linear Langevin dynamics on networks, we derive a mode decomposition for both the asymmetry of short-time cross-correlations and heat currents at steady state. This decomposition reveals two sources of nonequilibrium---fluctuations of individual modes and correlated fluctuations between distinct modes. For reciprocal networks with independent local driving, we derive two nonequilibrium response operators that yield explicit expressions for the global asymmetry intensity and the entropy production rate. These operators are weighted Laplacians independent of stochastic driving. Their spectra determine attainable upper and lower bounds on nonequilibrium at fixed driving heterogeneity. These bounds are exact for asymmetry intensity at arbitrary deviations from equilibrium and hold to leading order near equilibrium for entropy production rate. Finally, we find that the hierarchical modular organization of human structural connectomes broadens the brain's nonequilibrium operating range, with resting-state brain activity supporting this topological advantage for sustaining a lower nonequilibrium level. Our study provides a basis for understanding biological network organization and designing networks with targeted nonequilibrium operating points.
item.dc:creator: Dingjie Wu, Yaozu Wang, Rong Wang, Ying Wu

item.title: Dynamic scaling behaviors induced by periodic drivings at continuous Ising quantum transitions
item.description: arXiv:2611.32301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the out-of-equilibrium scaling behaviors induced by periodic driving protocols in quantum many-body systems near continuous quantum phase transitions at zero temperature. We consider two paradigmatic one-dimensional systems: the quantum Ising chain subject to periodic longitudinal fields and the Kitaev fermionic wire with periodically driven chemical potentials, equivalent to a quantum Ising chain with a periodic transverse field. Within a renormalization-group (RG) framework, we develop a dynamic scaling theory for both finite-size systems and the thermodynamic limit, identifying scaling variables associated with the driving amplitude and period. We distinguish between protocols that break the global ${\mathbb Z}_2$ symmetry by coupling to the order parameter and those that preserve it. These two classes of driving exhibit distinct scaling behaviors, with power-law exponents determined by the RG dimensions of the corresponding perturbations. We verify the proposed dynamic scaling theory through numerical simulations of both smooth single-frequency and discontinuous square-wave periodic drivings.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Pelissetto, Davide Rossini, Ettore Vicari

item.title: Classifying exact local-equilibrium solutions of the Boltzmann equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.32468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a complete classification, in a \(d\)-dimensional Euclidean space, of all hydrodynamic states and external forces for which a local equilibrium distribution constitutes an exact solution to the Boltzmann kinetic equation. We demonstrate that the temperature \(T\) must be spatially uniform, that the velocity field is the sum of a rigid translation, a radial expansion or compression, and a rigid rotation, and that the external acceleration must be conservative, though time-dependent within a reference frame that translates and rotates along with the fluid. The density profile is then determined by the external potential, while its temporal dependence is governed by any temperature function \(T(t)\) that can be generated through an appropriate adjustment of the external acceleration. We recover the classic ``harmonic breather'' and obtain solutions involving static forces that exhibit algebraic cooling, similar to Haff's law, despite the occurrence of elastic collisions. Our classification identifies the exceptional circumstances under which local equilibrium is exact and provides rigorous criteria for evaluating kinetic and hydrodynamic approximations.
item.dc:creator: Nagi Khalil, Jorge Bravo-Gadea

item.title: On fluctuation properties of the cumulative current in gTASEP on open chains
item.description: arXiv:2611.32495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present preliminary results of our numerical study of the fluctuation properties of the cumulative current, JT, in the generalized totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (gTASEP) on open chains with Liggett boundary conditions. GTASEP is the ordinary TASEP (a model of 1D- traffic on a single track, having many diverse applications), where an additional term controlling clustering of the particles is added. Extensive numerical simulations are performed to determine the dependence of the second scaled cumulant C2 of the time integrated current, JT, on the system size, L, in the long-time limit, allowing for comparison between open and periodic geometries. Preliminary results for C2 in the maximum current phase show agreement with theoretical predictions about the Kardar-Parizi-Zhang universality of the gTASEP on a segment.
item.dc:creator: N. C. Pesheva, N. Zh. Bunzarova, E. K. Mitsova, A. M. Povolotsky

item.title: Lattice models of chiral random motion: A short review
item.description: arXiv:2611.32743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chirality, a systematic rotational bias, is ubiquitous in many random motion patterns, from bacteria cells, that swim in circles near surfaces and spinning colloids, to charged particles diffusing under the influence of magnetic fields. In two dimensions, chirality renders random transport \textit{odd}: the diffusion tensor acquires an antisymmetric part that leaves the mean-squared displacement invariant but modifies fluxes and boundary currents. Lattice models for random motion are a natural setting to study chirality, since they are exactly solvable, connect directly to heterogeneous media, cellular automata, and programmable robots, and in discrete time admit fully chiral limits with a localised bulk and edge transport. Lattice walks with a rotational bias have been introduced in different communities several times since 1960, yet without a common language or conceptual connection between them. Here we review these models from the perspective that on the lattice, chirality requires memory. Taking the recently introduced chiral random walk model as a template, we describe the walker with an internal degree of freedom. With a chiral biased updating rule, the full diffusion tensor of this chiral walker turns odd. Within this picture, we can unite persistent and chiral walks, run-and-tumble motion, and cyclic random motions in one framework. We discuss how the memory is followed into the environment; in Lorentz lattice gases, kinetic and rotor walks, and random odd environments; and into the path; in spiral self-avoiding walks.
item.dc:creator: E. Kalz, J. Wojcik, N. Sherf, Y. Roichman, R. Metzler

item.title: Ordering Information in Multispecies Long-Range Swap Processes
item.description: arXiv:2611.32766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We measure how much the left-to-right species order $W_t$ of interacting particles on the integer lattice reveals about their initial configuration. For distinct species under long-range swaps, deleting stronger particles gives coordinates with independent Poisson increments. For a finitely supported initial law, the mutual information between any function $U$ of the initial configuration and $W_t$ is $C_U/t+O(t^{-3/2})$ as $t\to\infty$, where $C_U$, which may vanish, is determined by the means of Gaussian order statistics and the conditional means of the initial compressed coordinates given $U$. On consecutive sites with a uniform initial order, we compute the coefficient of the $t\log(1/t)$ term in the short-time information loss for arbitrary species counts. For three particles in this setting, repeating the weaker rather than the stronger species triples the long-time $t^{-1}$ coefficient, although both compositions have the same composition entropy and initial-order entropy. These long-time coefficients are the same whether equal particles block or push each other, but the nonuniform limiting output law is reversed. In the ordinary multispecies totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP), two distinct particles at fixed sites with a uniform initial order instead give $t^{-1/2}$ decay.
item.dc:creator: Eunghyun Lee

item.title: Entanglement Asymmetry and the Quantum Mpemba Effect in Inhomogeneous Quenches
item.description: arXiv:2611.32934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entanglement asymmetry is a powerful probe of symmetry breaking and its dynamical restoration following quantum quenches. While extensively studied for homogeneous initial states, its evolution from inhomogeneous initial configurations remains largely unexplored. We investigate a spin-$1/2$ XX chain whose two halves are initially prepared in tilted ferromagnetic states with different tilt angles. Combining generalized hydrodynamics (GHD) and the quasiparticle picture with exact fermionic correlation-matrix calculations, we study the dynamics of entanglement asymmetry. We find good agreement between the two approaches for generic initial configurations and observe the quantum Mpemba effect, whereby states with stronger initial symmetry breaking can restore the symmetry faster. This effect now depends on the subsystem position: while the homogeneous behavior is recovered when the subsystem lies entirely within one of the initially tilted halves, the entanglement-asymmetry curves for subsystems straddling the interface can exhibit multiple crossings or no crossings at all. A notable exception occurs for subsystems entirely within an initially non-tilted half. In this case, GHD predicts vanishing asymmetry, but the exact dynamics generates a small, nonzero asymmetry that can develop a plateau before decaying toward zero. This feature reveals contributions beyond the leading-order hydrodynamic description.
item.dc:creator: Ma\"elle Olivier, Filiberto Ares, Pasquale Calabrese

item.title: Anomalous front propagation in many-body quantum transport with memory-dependent resetting
item.description: arXiv:2611.32961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce an exactly solvable framework for non-Markovian quantum many-body dynamics based on stochastic resetting with memory. Applicable to arbitrary time-independent Hamiltonians, including interacting systems, our framework provides an exact representation of the dynamics with memory in terms of the corresponding reset-free evolution, which can be accessed either analytically or numerically. We demonstrate the power of this approach by studying domain-wall melting in a one-dimensional chain of noninteracting fermions, obtaining exact analytical results for the density profile, the local structure of the front edge, the extreme-value statistics of the rightmost fermion, and the integrated current. Remarkably, memory transforms ballistic transport into logarithmically slow propagation without arresting spreading. While the macroscopic density profile retains its original scaling function, the front edge broadens as $\sqrt{\ln t}$ rather than $t^{1/3}$ at late times and develops a qualitatively different edge structure. Furthermore, the extreme-value statistics change from Tracy--Widom to Gaussian, while both the mean and variance of the integrated current grow logarithmically in time. Our predictions are in excellent agreement with numerical simulations. These results reveal how memory can fundamentally alter quantum many-body transport and its fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: Gabriele de Mauro, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar

item.title: Energy transport from an active medium
item.description: arXiv:2611.32992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the energy current through a harmonic chain whose left end is coupled, via a short-range contact potential, to a medium of overdamped run-and-tumble particles moving on a ring, while the right end is attached to a zero-temperature Langevin reservoir. The activity is parametrized by the propulsion speed $v_0$ and the persistence time $\tau$. Using nonequilibrium response theory at weak system-medium coupling, we predict the stationary current and simulations reproduce it over a large part of the $(v_0,\tau)$ plane. That includes the possible nonmonotonicity of the current as function of $v_0$ and $\tau$, and occurrence of resonances with the normal modes of the chain, most significantly at large $\tau$ and small $v_0$. There is a critical propulsion speed $v_c$ at which the ring-crossing frequency of the particles leaves the phonon band: for $v_0<v_c$ the current grows with persistence, while for $v_0>v_c$ it decays as $(v_0^2\tau)^{-1}$. We also explain where the theoretical prediction fails, especially due to an oscillatory instability originating from a sufficiently strong negative friction induced on the leftmost oscillator. Finally, the persistent medium produces strongly non-Gaussian velocity statistics and long-range, oscillating velocity correlations in the bulk of the chain.
item.dc:creator: Simon Krekels, Christian Maes, Ion Santra

item.title: Systematic and accurate anharmonic formation free energies of metastable defects via a constrained Bayesian Adaptive Biasing Force framework
item.description: arXiv:2608.20902v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computing the formation free energies of metastable defects at finite temperature remains challenging due to anharmonicity, the multiplicity of basins and the frequent occurrence of migration events. Using the previously introduced constrained Bayesian Adaptive Biasing Force method (BABFc), we establish a practical thermodynamic integration framework for computing restricted anharmonic formation free energies associated with individual metastable defect basins. We demonstrate that BABFc can be exploited as a robust, systematic and numerically efficient tool for addressing a long standing bottleneck in atomistic materials science: the finite temperature thermodynamic characterization of metastable defects in complex, highly anharmonic energy landscapes. The proposed workflow requires only a reference local minimum and a confinement strategy and does not rely on defect specific collective variables. It therefore provides a general route to assign well-defined free energies to individual metastable basins, even when these basins are separated by low barriers and embedded in a dense landscape of competing configurations. In this setting, BABFc enables stable, bias corrected free energy estimates with statistical accuracies at the meV/atom level and a very low failure rate, including for systems containing approximately one thousand atoms. We demonstrate this capability through thousands of independent free energy calculations covering hundreds of four-interstitial and four-vacancy configurations in bcc $\alpha$-Fe over a broad temperature range, using both a traditional empirical potential and a data driven force field.
item.dc:creator: Clovis Lapointe, Anruo Zhong, Manuel Ath\`enes, Mihai-Cosmin Marinica

item.title: Locality from Nonlocality: Symmetry Relocalization and Gauging of Lattice Dirac Fermions
item.description: arXiv:2611.31366v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatially nonlocal symmetries need not imply nonlocal gauge dynamics. Nonlocal canonical transformations make certain exact nonlocal compact symmetries of free lattice Dirac fermions onsite while retaining sufficient Hamiltonian locality for gauging. Symmetry relocalization yields exact or emergent gauge locality in 1D, 2D, and 3D, subject to lattice structure, topology, and anomalies. In 1D, a Hamiltonian-preserving transformation exchanges onsite vector and nonlocal spectral axial charges of a half-filled chain, enabling local gauging of each and exposing their mixed anomaly. Bosonization identifies momentum-winding T-duality, with a parity-projected operator flowing to a noninvertible topological defect. A nonperturbative norm-resolvent bound proves emergent dynamical gauge locality at finite chemical potential, while a doubled Chern-insulator parent reveals the duality's bulk origin and superconducting extensions reveal hidden compact symmetries. In 2D, the square $\pi$-flux Majorana model shares the Kitaev honeycomb model's single Dirac fermion and odd Pfaffian parity but supports sharp and exponentially local compact charges, the latter with nontrivial Chern topology. Relocalization retains Schwartz locality for asymptotically local gauging, while AIII/AII parents clarify bulk charge origin and parity-anomaly inflow. Two flavors yield compact $U(2)$, a quaternionic invariant, and asymptotically local non-Abelian gauging. In 3D, an exact mixed vector-axial flux response is derived, while a distinct model supports an exponentially local vector $U(1)$ charge with strong quaternionic topology. A nonlocal map makes the charge and Kramers symmetry onsite while preserving exponential Hamiltonian locality. For a compact $SU(2)$ Weyl doublet, a no-go theorem forbids translation-preserving Gaussian onsite relocalization retaining Weyl content and Hamiltonian locality.
item.dc:creator: Lei Su

item.title: Ground-State Chiral Quantum Clusters
item.description: arXiv:2611.31370v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum time crystals are states of matter that spontaneously break time translation symmetry, extending the notion of crystalline order to time. While their out-of-equilibrium version has been successfully realized by periodic driving, the equilibrium counterpart remains elusive. Here we introduce "ground-state chiral quantum clusters": self-bound many-body ground states supporting a persistent current. We provide a minimal field theory describing these states, and an exact microscopic realization via the attractive anyonic Lieb-Liniger model on a ring. In the latter, the ground-state density-density correlator exhibits the Talbot effect, with a soliton-like profile that periodically disperses and revives while drifting indefinitely along the ring, realizing persistent motion at equilibrium. Possible experimental probes are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Massaro, Adolfo del Campo

item.title: Eigenvalue-based computation of Richardson pairing spectra and finite-size thermodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.31531v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a numerical workflow for the reduced BCS Richardson model, combining the eigenvalue-based Bethe equations, Baxter-polynomial reconstruction, and complex root finding. Newton-Raphson iteration solves the nonlinear equations for the eigenvalue-based variables; a linear system yields the polynomial coefficients, and Laguerre iteration with polynomial deflation extracts the rapidities. We apply the procedure to equally spaced, quadratic, and hydrogen-like non-degenerate single-particle spectra as the pairing strength varies. For finite systems, we calculate canonical observables from the complete seniority-zero spectrum and check benchmark spectra against exact diagonalization. In an eight-level, four-pair system with a hydrogen-like spectrum, the heat capacity has two maxima at weak coupling. With increasing coupling, the low-temperature maximum shifts upward and the high-temperature maximum downward; the latter ceases to be a distinct local maximum near $g\simeq0.03515$ in the units used. The equally spaced benchmark instead has a single dominant maximum over the coupling interval displayed for that spectrum. This comparison illustrates how single-particle level spacings can shape finite-size thermal response. The C++ code is publicly available; numerical instabilities remain possible near ill-conditioned configurations and at larger sizes.
item.dc:creator: Grzegorz Biskowski, Marcin R. Piatek, Franco Ferrari

item.title: Absence of $\sigma$-criticality in Short-Range Spin Glasses
item.description: arXiv:2611.31584v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The stability of ground states in the Edwards-Anderson Ising spin glass in dimensions two and higher against perturbations of a single coupling can be quantified through the ``flexibility'' of that coupling in a particular ground state. The property of $\sigma$-criticality is one in which varying a single coupling can alter the flexibilities of a (strictly) positive density of couplings in an infinite system, and its presence provides a sufficient condition for the presence of multiple ground state pairs. In a previous paper it was shown for the EA spin glass that $\sigma$-criticality of the first kind, in which the critical droplet of a bond has a positive-density interface with the ground state, was ruled out in any dimension. The remaining possibility, called $\sigma$-criticality of the second kind, is one in which a bond lies in the critical droplet boundaries of a positive density of other bonds. We show here that this kind of $\sigma$-criticality is also absent, ruling out altogether the presence of $\sigma$-criticality in the EA spin glass. While this doesn't resolve the question of multiplicity of ground state pairs, it removes a sufficient condition for its presence. We then propose a rigorous necessary condition for ground state pair multiplicity.
item.dc:creator: C. M. Newman, D. L. Stein

item.title: A colored look at anyons and parastatistics
item.description: arXiv:2611.31841v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Color Lie (super)algebras were introduced in 1978 by Rittenberg and Wyler as generalizations of ordinary Lie (super)algebras. These color structures, graded by abelian groups, are defined by brackets which satisfy generalized Jacobi identities. Only recently the relevance of color Lie (super)algebras to physical applications has been pointed out and proved. The color framework not only describes, but also provides physical signatures for two broad types of parastatistics (particles beyond ordinary bosons/fermions): i) paraparticles which are exchanged via the permutation group and can exist in any space dimension D and ii) anyons (exchanged via the braid group), which exist up to D=2 space dimensions. This paper presents an update of the recent advancements which motivate a brand new "colored look" at questions involving parastatistics and braid statistics.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Toppan

item.title: Relaxation dynamics of the impurity momentum in a one-dimensional Fermi gas
item.description: arXiv:2611.32280v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a single mobile impurity coupled by a repulsive contact interaction to a gas of free spinless fermions of equal mass in one dimension. Using the determinant overlaps between the interacting eigenstates and free-fermion states, we derive closed determinant formulas for the matrix elements of the impurity momentum operator and of its square between arbitrary Bethe-ansatz eigenstates of a finite system. At infinite coupling we prove a selection rule: both operators have vanishing matrix elements between distinct eigenstates that share the same rapidity, and every eigenstate carries the per-particle share of the total momentum. For an impurity injected into the Fermi sea we have the following: at infinite coupling the average impurity momentum relaxes completely in the thermodynamic limit, while at finite coupling relaxation remains incomplete. The closed-form matrix elements turn the spectral representation of the average impurity momentum into explicit finite sums over eigenstates. We evaluate the post-injection dynamics, resolve the quantum-flutter oscillations and the approach towards the diagonal-ensemble value, and map the stationary momentum as a function of the injection momentum and the coupling. Finally, we analyse the thermodynamic limit and its asymptotics as an integral over Fredholm determinants.
item.dc:creator: Felipe Taha Sant'Ana

item.title: Correlation functions of 2D critical models via a KPZ relation for conformal blocks
item.description: arXiv:2611.32485v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Knizhnik--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (KPZ) relation allows scaling exponents of two-dimensional (2D) critical systems to be derived from their counterparts in Liouville quantum gravity. We extend this framework to correlation functions based on an integral inversion relation between Virasoro conformal blocks with complementary central charges $c$ and $26-c$. We demonstrate this method in various models by deriving the 2-point disk correlation from their quantum counterpart and the KPZ relation. Results on critical loop models were previously known, but our method is robust enough to include many scenarios previously unsolved, such as the Fuzzy Potts model. Our approach is complementary to the conformal bootstrap.
item.dc:creator: Gefei Cai, Shengzhi Jin, Xin Sun, Baojun Wu

item.title: Odd Viscosity-Driven Phase Separation in Chiral Active Mixtures
item.description: arXiv:2611.32535v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Binary mixtures of active particles spinning in opposite directions can spontaneously separate into homochiral domains, yet the mechanism behind this robust demixing remains poorly understood. Here, we establish a two-fluid hydrodynamic theory that generalizes odd viscosity to multicomponent systems. We show that cross parity-violating viscosities, which couple the stress of one chiral species to the strain rate of another, can destabilize the homogeneous mixture, while odd viscosity within each homochiral domain governs the interfacial stability and dynamics. Microscopic measurements of stress and velocity correlations yield viscosity estimates that predict spontaneous demixing followed by domain coarsening. These findings identify odd viscosity as a route to programming phase behavior and domain morphology in chiral active mixtures.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyi Wu, Tzer Han Tan, Hongbo Zhao

item.title: Thermodynamics of complex crystals from a generalized mean-field bond model
item.description: arXiv:2611.32609v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend our previously introduced mean-field bond model from unary fcc lattices to crystals with multiple chemical species and sublattices, accurately predicting finite-temperature thermodynamics without statistical sampling. Our generalization reformulates the model in terms of the Wyckoff positions of the crystal, representing each by one atom, and solving for the bond density of the reference bond of each of its neighbor shells. Bond-bond correlation functions are built from the zero-temperature force constants, allowing the deviation of every bond in the crystal to be expressed through linear functions of the reference bond of a shell. Thermodynamic self-consistency is enforced by requiring a single virial temperature for the whole crystal, and compatibility of average bond lengths with crystal volume. Model predictions are validated against molecular dynamics simulations of unary, binary, and ternary crystals using Morse-type bonding potentials, parametrized for each shell from the force constants of empirical interatomic potentials at several isotropic strains. In each case, the predicted bond densities and thermodynamics agree with the simulations to within their statistical uncertainty. We discuss strategies for combining the model with bonding potentials parametrized from first principles and foundation models to predict the finite-temperature thermodynamics of complex crystals at ab initio accuracy without statistical sampling.
item.dc:creator: Raynol Dsouza, Thomas D. Swinburne, J\"org Neugebauer

item.title: Conformality lost in Anderson localization in infinite dimensions, and regained in finite dimensions: a phenomenological theory of the Anderson transition in high dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.32725v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the recent works on Anderson localization when the number of spatial dimensions $d\to\infty$ can be framed into the scenario dubbed it conformality lost [Kaplan et al., Phys. Rev. D 80, 125005 (2009)], which occurs when two fixed points of the RG collide and become complex. This framing makes it natural for a two-parameter scaling flow \`a la Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT) to control all the observables of the theory as conjectured in [Vanoni et al., PNAS 121, e2401955121 (2024)]. We also use this as a starting point for an $\epsilon$ expansion of the RG equations in $\epsilon=1/d\ll 1$, and find phenomenological RG equations which fit the numerical results in dimensions $d\gtrsim 4$.
item.dc:creator: Antonello Scardicchio, Carlo Vanoni

item.title: Recovery of Extended Modes from the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect Due to Local Nonlinearity on a Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2611.32783v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Localization in continuum spectra known as the non-Hermitian skin effect is widely believed to be a consequence of nontrivial topology of bulk bands. However, the robustness of the non-Hermitian skin effect against nonlinear effects is still a nontrivial problem. We here reveal that single-bond nonlinearity on a boundary can recover extended modes in a non-Hermitian tight-binding model. We propose and analyze a one-dimensional minimal model, where we introduce a nonlinear phase shift of a hopping term only at boundary sites. We also propose a possible photonic setup to dynamically observe the nonlinearity-induced extended modes as a steady state. Our results thus challenge the conventional notion of the non-Hermitian skin effect by revealing its dependence on nonlinear boundary conditions.
item.dc:creator: Kazuki Sone, Tomonari Mizoguchi, Yasuhiro Hatsugai

item.title: From Fermions to Vortices: Microscopic Simulations of Phase Ordering in a d-Wave Superconductor
item.description: arXiv:2611.32916v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Describing bath-induced superconducting phase ordering directly from a microscopic fermionic Hamiltonian remains a formidable challenge. Here we develop a microscopic framework for this problem using the recently introduced adiabatic variational principle (AVP) and demonstrate its application to a two-dimensional $d$-wave superconductor. The central construction maps evolving, spatially inhomogeneous bond-pairing fields onto constrained Bogoliubov-de Gennes states, with the associated Lagrange multipliers determining the thermodynamic driving forces. This enables dissipative evolution of the superconducting order while retaining its microscopic electronic structure, without assuming a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau free-energy functional. Starting from disordered pairing configurations, we resolve the emergence of phase coherence through vortex-antivortex annihilation and the accompanying evolution of local electronic spectra. Vortex decay and dynamical scaling recover the characteristic kinetics of two-dimensional phase ordering, providing a nontrivial benchmark of the framework. The solver-independent AVP formulation opens a route to microscopic studies of dissipative ordering and metastability in superconductors with intertwined stripe and pair-density-wave orders.
item.dc:creator: Ali Rayat, Gia-Wei Chern

item.title: Confinement-induced Transitions of Chiral Active Particles and Dumbbells
item.description: arXiv:2611.32972v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a coherent framework for the stochastic description of a chiral Active Brownian Particle (cABP) and a chiral Active Brownian Dumbbell (cABD) in a harmonic trap. On the one hand, we employ the Martin-Siggia-Rose path integral formalism, using the passive Brownian motion as a reference state around which activity is accounted for as a perturbation series in the self-propulsion speed. This method is suited best to calculate the exact time-dependent correlation functions. On the other hand, we use the Fokker-Planck equation, which works best to obtain the steady-state probability distribution. We discuss in detail the transitions from a trap centered distribution for low activity/strong confinement to a ring-shaped distribution for high activity/low confinement and the effect of chirality, i.e. the active angular velocity. For the dumbbell, a series of such transitions occurs and the correlation functions yield information about the particle's conformation and orientation. This establishes the combined framework as a powerful tool to investigate stochastic active particle systems.
item.dc:creator: Mike Brandt, Falko Ziebert, Carsten Littek

item.title: Local Thermodynamic Reconstruction of Impurity Entropy
item.description: arXiv:2611.32974v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Resolving the thermodynamic entropy associated with a local impurity in a spatially extended interacting quantum bath remains a numerical challenge. We develop a Local-Maxwell approach that reconstructs the impurity entropy from local observables in worldline quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations. By integrating their temperature responses along the impurity coupling, the method avoids separate estimates of extensive entropies. For nonnegative worldline expansions with bounded local couplings, we establish bath-size independent bounds on all factorial moments of the impurity vertex count. For even vertex counts, the Maxwell estimator variance remains bounded as the coupling approaches zero. The transverse-field Ising benchmark reproduces exact free fermion results, while an interacting XXZ chain demonstrates up to several hundredfold improvement in statistical efficiency over conventional extensive thermodynamic integration. In a three-channel XXZ impurity junction, we reveal entropy recovery upon cooling and a nonmonotonic coupling dependence of the finite-temperature entropy contrast. These results establish local thermodynamic reconstruction as an efficient approach to impurity entropy in interacting quantum baths.
item.dc:creator: Hang Su

item.title: Polar Streams through Active Condensation in Flocks
item.description: arXiv:2611.33007v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Two of the most paradigmatic phenomena in active matter are flocking, where particles align to move collectively, and motility-induced phase separation, where self-propulsion causes particles to condense even without attractive interactions. Here, using experiments on self-propelled Janus colloid dimers, we show that flocks can phase separate to form polar streams. These structures are elongated dense clusters of particles that flock along the stream's long axis, in contrast to the well-known transverse bands that form close to the flocking transition. We use particle-based simulations and hydrodynamic theory obtained through coarse-graining to identify the underlying mechanism, which we call active nematic condensation: Denser regions of the flock develop stronger polar and hence nematic order, which leads to further particle fluxes into the dense region. These results reveal a generic mechanism whereby flocks can condense into streams. Our findings uncover that flocks can be shaped by nematic order, which is usually not accounted for in the standard Toner-Tu equations. More broadly, our work shows that collective motion and phase separation can not only coexist but also cooperate in active matter.
item.dc:creator: Lauritz Hahn, Xinyu Dou, Ziqi Zhou, Jie Zhang, Marin Bukov, Ricard Alert

item.title: A model colloidal gel former for the measurement of inter-particle forces
item.description: arXiv:2611.33091v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tracking of particle coordinates in colloidal model systems is an established technique. Recently, an emulsion system has been introduced where not only the coordinates, but also contacts and compressive forces between the droplets can be determined [Dong et al. J. Chem. Phys. 156 214907 (2022). Here we develop this system to control both the density mismatch and refractive index contrast between the emulsion droplets and the solvent. The former is important in minimizing sedimentation due to gravity and the latter is necessary for 3d imaging with confocal microscopy. By mapping our system carefully to computer simulation, we quantify interdroplet forces and packing geometries in depletion gels and probe the relationship between local structure and compressive stress. The simulations also provide ensemble measurements of the attractive part of the force between droplets and related quantities such as the stress tensor. Finally, we implement an improved measure of local stress in our experiments, which can be directly compared with the corresponding quantity in simulations. We find that locally rigid minimum energy clusters are associated with regions of higher stress in the gel network.
item.dc:creator: Rui Cheng, Kristian Thijssen, Abraham Mauleon Amieva, Tanniemola B. Liverpool, Malcolm A. Faers, Robert L. Jack, C. Patrick Royall

item.title: Topological insulators on site-eliminated, projected, and patterned fractal lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.33155v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Identifying fractal lattices of fractional (Hausdorff) dimension as geometric descendants of parent crystals, we showcase the successful realization of canonical topological insulators in one-, two-, and three-dimensional crystals on their self-similar descents using three complementary approaches, starting from lattice-regularized models in integer dimensions. (a) In the first approach, we construct the fractal Hamiltonian by removing all parent-lattice sites that do not belong to such a network (method of site elimination). (b) In the second one, we integrate or project out the same set of sites to obtain an effective Hamiltonian for the fractal lattice (method of projection or renormalization). (c) In the third approach, we retain the parent-crystal lattice intact but spatially pattern the on-site mass parameter, which controls the topology of the parent insulating system, such that it assumes two topologically distinct values on the fractal network and its complement (patterned fractal lattices). By numerically diagonalizing the resulting Hamiltonians and computing appropriate topological invariants or local markers, corroborating the bulk-boundary correspondence through gapless modes at outer or inner boundaries, we establish Su-Schrieffer-Heeger topology on the Cantor set using all three approaches, Haldane topology on the hexaflake [using (a) and (b)] and Qi-Wu-Zhang topology on the Sierpi\'nski carpet [using (c)], and strong $Z_2$ topological insulating phases on the tiled Menger sponge from methods (a), (b), and (c). These findings complement and substantially extend the previously reported realization of Qi-Wu-Zhang topology on the Sierpi\'nski carpet using methods (a) and (b) [Phys. Rev. B 110, L241302 (2024)].
item.dc:creator: Aiden Mains, Danile Salib, Christopher Leong, Bitan Roy

item.title: Time arrow in open-boundary one-dimensional stochastic dynamics: effects of discrete thermal kicks over temperature interface
item.description: arXiv:2507.09145v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Does nonequilibrium characteristics exhibit in one-dimensional open-boundary stochastic systems? We introduce a discrete-timestep stochastic model, where the particle dynamics follows a discrete overdamped stochastic equation, and thermal kicks are presented over discrete timesteps. These thermal kicks are derived from a position-dependent temperature profile with a sharp interface. The discrete characteristic and the It\^{o}-type stochastic scheme make our model distinct from the conventional discussions of an overdamped colloidal model. Under the open-boundary condition, one cannot observe any net probability current in the nonequilibrium steady state (NESS). On the other hand, the nonequilibrium nature of this system can be extracted through the asymmetry in forward and backward transition probabilities, as is reported in this work through the simulation and theoretic analysis. In particular, our result shows prominent time irreversibility near the temperature interface. We propose a hidden-gyration scenario that demonstrates the source of irreversibility, while the collapse of gyrations on the one-dimensional coordinate accounts for the absence of probability current.
item.dc:creator: Chi-Lun Lee, Yu-Syuan Lin, Pik-Yin Lai

item.title: Time irreversibility and entropy production in non-Hermitian Model A field theories
item.description: arXiv:2603.11450v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a systematic framework to quantify irreversibility in scalar Model A field theories with a generic non-Hermitian term driving the dynamics. Using the stochastic path-integral formalism, we perform a controlled small-noise expansion, allowing the computation of the entropy production rate (EPR) and violations of the fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT). We show that the local EPR is entirely determined by the anti-Hermitian part of the linearised Langevin equation. Around steady states, the non-Hermitian component produces linear corrections to FDT violations and contributes quadratically to the EPR. As an illustration of the applicability of our approach, we analyse a minimal non-Hermitian extension of the Ginzburg-Landau $\psi^4$ theory describing a non-reciprocal Ising model at coarse-grained scales, for which we obtain explicit expressions of the local EPR, showing that it localises at interfaces in non-uniform states. Our results provide a general characterisation of TRS breaking in non-Hermitian scalar field theories.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Carosi, Ot Garc\'es, Adri\`a Garc\'es, Demian Levis

item.title: Mean-field theory of myopic self-avoiding fractional Brownian motion
item.description: arXiv:2606.13972v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Myopic self-avoiding fractional Brownian motion (FBM) is a stochastic process in which an ensemble of particles is driven by fractional Gaussian noise while being repelled by the gradient of the time-integrated ensemble density [J. House et al., Phys. Rev. E 112, 034119 (2025)]. Depending on the anomalous diffusion exponent $\alpha$ characterizing the noise, the process features two dynamical regimes: an interaction-dominated regime ($\alpha < \alpha_c=4/(d+2)$) where the mean-density interaction governs long-time dynamics, and a noise-dominated regime ($\alpha > \alpha_c$) where FBM correlations prevail. In the interaction-dominated regime, the mean-squared displacement grows as $\langle r^2(t) \rangle \sim t^{4/(d+2)}$ regardless of $\alpha$, while for $\alpha > \alpha_c$ the standard FBM scaling $\langle r^2(t) \rangle \sim t^{\alpha}$ is recovered. Here, we develop an analytical mean-field theory of myopic self-avoiding FBM, based on a Fokker-Planck approach to the interaction-dominated regime. This allows us to derive closed-form polynomial solutions for the probability density. To compare with computer simulations, we develop an efficient radial binning algorithm that significantly reduces the computational complexity, making large-scale three-dimensional simulations feasible. Extensive simulations in one, two, and three dimensions confirm the analytical predictions. We also discuss the application of the process to the self-organization of serotonergic axons (fibers) in vertebrate brains, where FBM paths with self-avoidance provide a natural framework for understanding spatial heterogeneities of fiber densities.
item.dc:creator: Rashad Bakhshizada, Skirmantas Janu\v{s}onis, Ralf Metzler, Thomas Vojta

item.title: Cyclic machines in contact with thermal and athermal baths: the role of Poisson shot noise
item.description: arXiv:2606.29838v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study stochastic models of a microscopic active heat engine, comprised of an overdamped Brownian particle trapped in a harmonic potential, and in simultaneous contact with thermal (passive) and athermal (active) baths. The interaction with the active bath is modeled as a stochastic force described by Poisson shot-noise (PSN) having a specified amplitude distribution. With analytical calculations and numerical simulations, we study the thermodynamic performance of this machine with cyclic protocols that are analogous to two-stroke and Stirling-like engines. For specific parameter ranges, the thermodynamic behavior is that of a hybrid machine, operating as a heat engine with respect to the thermal (passive) bath and as a refrigerator with respect to the PSN (active) bath, or vice versa. Focusing on the parameter region where the overall performance is that of an engine, we show that the average total extracted work per cycle divided by average total heat intake from the hot baths per cycle may surpass the Carnot efficiency associated with the temperature of the passive baths. Applying the second law for active heat engines, we focus on a bonafide efficiency (bounded by Carnot's efficiency) that incorporates an information-theoretic metric~$\mathcal{I}$ ---which we call {\em quasistatic divergence}--- quantifying how distinguishable are the engine's statistics in the quasistatic limit with respect to a continually changing equilibrium distribution. We analyze, with theory and numerical simulations, how the PSN shot rate and the degree of non-Gaussianity in the particle position distribution influence the efficiency of the engine, and explore the correlation between non-Gaussianity and efficiency. Our findings reveal optimal PSN shot rates maximizing the engine's efficiency and an intriguing non-bijective relation between efficiency and kurtosis.
item.dc:creator: Rita Majumdar, Costantino Di Bello, Ralf Metzler, Rahul Marathe, \'Edgar Rold\'an

item.title: Seven- and eight-loop critical exponents of the three-dimensional Ising model
item.description: arXiv:2607.07776v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the critical exponents $\eta$, $\nu$, and the correction-to-scaling exponent $\omega$ of the three-dimensional Ising universality class by resumming the recently computed seven- and eight-loop renormalization-group series in the $\epsilon=4-d$ expansion [O.~Schnetz, \textit{Phys. Rev. D} \textbf{97}, 085018 (2018); O.~Schnetz, \textit{Phys. Rev. D} \textbf{107}, 036002 (2023)]. The resummation combines conformal mapping with a homographic transformation, while the resummation parameters are optimized according to two complementary criteria. This approach yields precise estimates of the critical exponents together with quantitative uncertainty estimates. We find that the error bar on $\eta$ decreases rapidly with increasing loop order, whereas this is the case neither for $\nu$ nor for $\omega$. Unexpectedly, although the estimated values are accurate in absolute terms, their slow convergence with the loop order leads to a slight but systematic tension with the conformal bootstrap estimates that are currently considered as the benchmark. We discuss several possible origins of this behavior and its implications for high-order resummations of perturbative renormalization-group series.
item.dc:creator: D. Shapoval, Yu. Honchar, B. Delamotte, M. Dudka, Yu. Holovatch

item.title: Memory-Retaining RG Fixed Points in Nonlinear PDEs
item.description:
arXiv:2607.14388v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Self-similar solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) are often interpreted as fixed points of renormalization-group (RG) transformations. Let $\xi$ denote a similarity variable and $\eta$ a dimensionless physical scale. In conventional RG descriptions, asymptotic coarse graining leads to memory loss, whereby $\eta$ disappears from the fixed-point solution. Here, we develop an RG framework in which fixed points take the general form $\eta^{\alpha}\Gamma(\xi/\eta^{ eta})$, where the surviving scale $\eta$ remains embedded in the asymptotic solution. While the case $ eta=0$ with $\alpha
eq 0$, corresponding to anomalous scaling via amplitude renormalization $\eta^{\alpha}$, is well understood within RG theory, self-similar solutions with $ eta
eq 0$ are known in second-kind self-similarity but have lacked a general RG formulation. We develop a nonperturbative RG framework for nonlinear PDEs that extends RG fixed-point theory to the $ eta
eq 0$ class by treating physical scales as dynamical variables of the RG flow. This framework identifies which scales remain asymptotically relevant and leads naturally to three classes of RG fixed points: memory-loss, memory-retaining I, and memory-retaining II. In the first class, scale information disappears asymptotically; in the second, it survives only in multiplicative amplitude factors such as $\eta^{\alpha}$; and in the third ($ eta
eq 0$), it remains embedded in the similarity profile $\Gamma$ itself. We illustrate the framework using conservative diffusion, the Barenblatt diffusion equation, a modified density-dependent diffusion model, and a three-scale fatigue-crack-growth problem. These examples show how RG flows determine both the surviving scales and the asymptotic self-similar solution, providing a unified RG formulation for memory retention and second-kind self-similarity with $ eta
eq 0$.
item.dc:creator: Ko Okumura

item.title: Activity-induced response amplification and instability near jamming in a Wishart--Ginibre model
item.description: arXiv:2607.26406v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the linear mechanical response of a disordered contact network using an additive Wishart--Ginibre model: a passive Wishart operator is perturbed by an independent real Ginibre coupling of strength \(\alpha_0\). The observable is the mean-square static displacement response per degree of freedom, normalized by the variance of the applied isotropic forces, rather than a shear compliance. In the large-matrix limit, the Hermitized Dyson equation gives \(J=(1-q)^{-3}/[1-(\alpha_0/\alpha_c)^2]\) on the stable side, where \(q<1\) is the Wishart aspect ratio and \(\alpha_c=(1-q)^{3/2}\). Thus the random coupling amplifies the response up to the onset of linear instability. At the unshifted isostatic point \(q=1\), the limiting spectrum enters the right half-plane for every nonzero \(\alpha_0\), so there is no stable isostatic susceptibility at nonzero activity. Direct matrix calculations show response amplification away from the threshold and a broadened stability crossover at finite size. Near marginality, a single singular value often carries much of the inverse trace, including in unstable realizations for which that trace is not a steady response.
item.dc:creator: Hisao Hayakawa

item.title: Geometric Propulsion of a Scallop with Control-Dependent Hydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2608.24158v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a force-free single-hinge swimmer driven by two controls. When its axial hydrodynamic connection depends only on the opening angle, we show that the mean displacement per cycle vanishes in the periodic state at any driving rate. An independent control of the hydrodynamic response removes this restriction. For a factorized connection, the displacement at arbitrary driving rate is an integral of a measurable shape moment against the hydrodynamic modulation; in the slow-driving limit it reduces to a curvature flux which, at fixed potential and connection, is independent of the shape mobility. A reflecting harmonic model illustrates how thermal fluctuations modify this flux without generating it, and a hinged-bead model with variable passive slip gives a quantitative opening--closing test of the mechanism. We distinguish these propulsion results from the leading shape-sector dissipation, which depends on the mobility and is governed by a thermodynamic metric.
item.dc:creator: Hisao Hayakawa

item.title: Foundations of Many-Body Theory of Quantum Unified Statistics: Green functions and Linear Response Theory
item.description: arXiv:2609.05878v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a comprehensive many-body theory for systems of particles obeying quantum unified statistics, or quons. After exploring the properties of the Fock space of this system, we formulate a systematic S-matrix expansion and a generalized Wick's theorem. A consistent Green-function formalism is constructed at both zero and finite temperatures, accompanied by a generalized Wick's theorem appropriate for infinite-statistics operator algebras. Within this framework, we establish diagrammatic rules for interacting quon systems. Employing the random phase approximation, we derive the dielectric function and reveal the emergence of anomalous plasmon modes that have no direct counterpart in conventional Bose or Fermi systems. We further analyze the ground-state energy, energy-loss function, generalized Thomas-Fermi screening wave vectors, and Friedel oscillations, elucidating how infinite statistics qualitatively modifies collective behavior and screening properties.
item.dc:creator: M. Beyrami, M. N. Najafi, H. Esmaili, M. Dournama, H. Mohammadzadeh

item.title: A JT/KPZ correspondence
item.description: arXiv:2511.02529v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We point out a correspondence between the Jackiw--Teitelboim (JT) gravity and the stationary measure of the Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) equation on an interval. By relating the Schwarzian limit of the double-scaled SYK to the weakly asymmetric limit of the open ASEP, we establish that the path-integral measure defining the Euclidean evolution between two end-of-the-world branes in JT gravity can be interpreted as the stationary measure of the KPZ equation on an interval with Neumann boundary conditions. We also establish the match between correlation functions.
item.dc:creator: Masataka Watanabe

item.title: Approximate Decoherence, Recoherence and Records in Isolated Quantum Systems
item.description: arXiv:2601.19703v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using the framework of decoherent histories, we study which past events leave detectable records in isolated quantum systems under the realistic assumption that decoherence is approximate and not perfect. Using tools from quantum state discrimination, we establish asymptotically for a large class of (pseudo-)random histories how the strength of decoherence changes the number of reliable records, i.e., we quantitatively answer the question: when can approximate decoherence be approximated by exact decoherence? In addition, we reveal a clear decoherence structure for long histories based on a numerically exact solution of a random matrix model that, as we argue, captures generic aspects of decoherence. In particular, we observe strong recoherences for maverick histories that are statistical outliers with respect to Born's rule. From the perspective of the Many Worlds Interpretation, our results reveal a "branch selection problem" and shed light on the emergence of Born's rule and the theory confirmation problem.
item.dc:creator: Philipp Strasberg, Joseph Schindler, Jiaozi Wang, Andreas Winter

item.title: Frustrated neurons: Energy landscapes and relaxation dynamics in repulsive phase oscillators
item.description: arXiv:2606.02512v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Geometrical frustration, a central paradigm in condensed matter physics, provides a unifying language for systems in which locally preferred interactions cannot be made globally compatible. Here, we use this language to formulate a minimal theory of frustrated neural timing, mapping repulsively coupled rhythmic units onto antiferromagnetic $XY$ models. In this formulation, the condensed-matter concepts of local constraints, degenerate ground-state manifolds, metastability, and quench dynamics are used to guide our analysis of structured neural phase dynamics. This paper analyzes a hierarchy of geometries, beginning with a triangle as the minimal frustrated motif with two chiral 120{\deg} timing states, then a tetrahedron whose reduced ground-state manifold consists of intersecting continuous branches associated with antipodal pairings, and finally a kagome lattice on which local constraints define a constrained three-coloring manifold. The kagome lattice reveals that zero-temperature relaxation suppresses global synchrony but typically selects low-energy metastable torque-balanced states rather than exact ground states. We then show how the phase theory can be carried back towards biophysical neural models by treating the minimal framework as an effective-interaction target, where geometrical timing frustration arises from preferred phase lags that become incompatible around closed motifs. Our results suggest that weak global coherence in neural systems doesn't necessarily signal disordered activity, but can instead reflect structured local timing order within a frustrated dynamical landscape.
item.dc:creator: Brandon B. Le

item.title: Quantum-echo Markov process for combinatorial optimization
item.description: arXiv:2609.38943v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a quantum-echo Markov process for combinatorial optimization. Quantum dynamics based on quantum annealing (QA) or the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is used to engineer the transition kernel. Increasing the annealing time in QA or the number of layers in QAOA enables transitions to explore distant configurations while suppressing large energy changes. The Hamming-space delocalization originates from operator spreading, whereas the energy-space localization arises from a dynamically generated correlation. For optimization, we propose quantum-echo local optimization. For the ferromagnetic Ising chain, increasing the annealing time or circuit depth yields a nearly quadratic improvement in the dependence of the mean first-passage time on the inverse optimality gap compared with random single-spin flips. For the random Ising model, increasing these parameters initially improves optimization performance, whereas further increases degrade performance in QA and lead to saturation in QAOA. Quantum-echo greedy descent substantially improves the performance, highlighting the complementary roles of quantum dynamics in exploration and greedy descent in exploitation. These results establish quantum-echo dynamics as a framework for engineering structured transition kernels and provide a route to using finite-resource quantum many-body dynamics as a computational primitive for iterative optimization.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuhiko Shirai

item.title: Finite-time quantum equilibration from local correlations
item.description: arXiv:2610.16351v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study equilibration of a fixed subsystem coupled to an initially maximally mixed bath. We show that the worst-input mean-square error, maximised over observation windows of length $T$, is bounded from above and below by the mean square of a complete local autocorrelation on $[0,T]$. The constants depend only on the subsystem dimension, and no assumption on degeneracies of energies or energy gaps is required. Subtracting the stationary part of the correlation gives equilibration to the temporal state; retaining it gives thermalisation to the maximally mixed state. We then obtain explicit bounds for two static Hamiltonian families. A periodic spin-clock model thermalises on $O(n\log n)$ windows at fixed accuracy despite an exponentially small positive energy. A randomly dressed commuting model, with interaction range $O(\log N)$, has expected error $O(N^{-b}+T^{-1})$ while retaining an extensive family of conserved observables. We explain how the locally weighted spectrum determines these bounds.
item.dc:creator: Piotr \'Cwikli\'nski

item.title: Microphase Separation and Ionic Aggregation in Oppositely Charged End-Functionalized Polymer Blends
item.description: arXiv:2610.24361v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using an ion-correlation-augmented self-consistent field theory (IC-SCFT), we study the phase behavior of binary blends of A and B polymers carrying single end groups of opposite charge. Under the low dielectric conditions typical for organic polymer melts, strong ion correlations drive association of multiple chain ends, leading to emergent multichain architectures that go beyond a simple ion-paired diblock copolymer picture previously used to interpret recent experiments. At moderate to strong polymer segregation, the resulting phase diagram differs considerably from this effective-diblock prediction: ion clustering broadens the lamellar and cylindrical windows while suppressing the network phases, the reverse of the trend for end-charged diblock copolymers. At weak segregation, the two polymers remain miscible even as ion clustering persists, and decreasing chain length drives the clusters themselves through a sphere-to-cylinder-to-lamella shape transition, connecting continuously to the aggregation behavior of classical terminally charged ionomers in the limit when one of the polymer species shrinks to just the charged end. These results reveal that ion clustering - beyond simple pairwise bonding - shapes the self-assembly of end-charged polymer blends.
item.dc:creator: Chao Duan, Zhen-Gang Wang

item.title: Atom as an Agent: Emergent Order by Collective Predictive Coding
item.description: arXiv:2610.36673v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: What is the intrinsic reason of emergence of macroscopic order parameter out of microscopic systems? In this article, we apply to physics the collective predictive coding (CPC), the theory of language/symbol emergence. As our language emerges out of our human communications, physical macroscopic order parameter emerges out of communications among atoms --- each atom is regarded as an agent who predicts each other's behavior through inference. We present three examples of classical spin systems: two-dimensional ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Ising models, a two-dimensional spin model with competing stripe orders, and the fully connected Sherrington--Kirkpatrick spin-glass model. In all of these examples, proper macroscopic order parameters including the replica overlap emerge automatically through communication informatics of CPC, only from observed spin configurations. We call the learned macroscopic coordinate the collective predictive order. Furthermore, for the ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Ising models, the equilibrium distribution of the collective predictive order yields an emergent potential with the symmetry and thermal evolution characteristic of a Landau potential. Notably, the emergence of the collective predictive order does not refer to any structure of microscopic Hamiltonians/Lagrangians. Thus our ``Atom-as-an-Agent" (AaaA) principle offers a completely data-driven method for the emergence of macroscopic order, that is, machine learning physics.
item.dc:creator: Koji Hashimoto, Tadahiro Taniguchi

item.title: Suppression of gel formation by spontaneous fragmentation
item.description: arXiv:2611.09537v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work we study the discrete Smoluchowski equation with a multiplicative kernel and an additional term describing the spontaneous shattering of each particle into monomers at a constant rate $\lambda$. We show that the introduction of fragmentation suppresses gelation for $\lambda \ge 4$. We derive analytical expressions for the second moment and the monomer concentration $n_1(t)$. These expressions lead to a recurrence relation allowing the steady-state particle size distribution for $\lambda \ge 4$ to be calculated with machine precision. We validate our analytical and semi-analytical results via numerical simulations using a solver that employs the Fast Fourier Transform for computation of the right-hand side and a second-order Runge-Kutta method with adaptive time steps.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Matveev

item.title: Open Quantum Time Crystals without External Thermodynamic Resources: Go and No-Go Theorems
item.description: arXiv:2611.09540v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Time crystals are phases of matter that spontaneously break time-translation symmetry. They have been ruled out in the ground and Gibbs states of isolated systems with only short-range interactions, yet they have been proposed and observed experimentally in nonequilibrium settings such as Floquet and open systems. However, existing proposals for time crystals in open quantum systems require an external supply of thermodynamic resources, such as work or energetic coherence. Whether coupling to an environment, without any such resource supply, can activate a time crystal absent in the isolated system remains open. We answer this question systematically through a Go theorem and a no-go theorem. The Go theorem answers it affirmatively: we construct an explicit model in which coupling a system to a zero-temperature Gibbs environment via a time-independent, energy-conserving interaction, with only short-range Hamiltonians, activates a time crystal in a stationary state that shows none in isolation. This coupling reproduces a Lindblad master equation satisfying three conditions---time-independent Hamiltonian and jump operators, time-translation covariance, and detailed balance---that hold in standard derivations unless thermodynamic resources are supplied externally. The no-go theorem shows that, for every Lindblad master equation satisfying these conditions and every stationary state, dissipation can never contribute to activation; only an environment-induced Hamiltonian term can. Indeed, the periodic two-time correlation function of any such time crystal coincides with that of the isolated system with the open-system Hamiltonian, the sum of the bare isolated Hamiltonian and the environment-induced Hamiltonian, in the thermodynamic limit. These results reveal both the possibility and the origin of time crystals in open systems without external resource supply.
item.dc:creator: Yuri Ogami, Hiroyasu Tajima

item.title: Quasi-particle sector hybridization and the onset of chaos in spin ladders
item.description: arXiv:2611.19053v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: How quasiparticle numbers influence the emergence of quantum chaos is a fundamental question in interacting many-body systems. We investigate this interplay in a spin-$1/2$ XXZ ladder, where the strong-rung regime supports an approximate organization of many-body eigenstates into quasi-particle(triplon) number sectors. Using spectral statistics, triplon-based observables, and von Neumann entanglement entropy, we characterize the microscopic hybridization of triplon-number sectors as the leg coupling increases. We find that the crossover toward Gaussian orthogonal ensemble statistics shifts to weaker couplings with increasing system size, whereas the characteristic crossover scale associated with triplon-sector hybridization exhibits a much weaker size dependence. Furthermore, eigenstate-to-eigenstate fluctuations exhibit scaling consistent with the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis even while remnants of the strong-rung structure persist, suggesting that spectral chaos does not necessarily require complete sector hybridization.
item.dc:creator: Arnav Pushkar, Abhik Kumar Saha
